title: Wigs on the green
html_source:
Humorous old phrase meaning a fracas or violent confrontation, chiefly Irish. It originated in the 1700s when wigs were part of the typical male costume. Back then, if a fight were to break out, the combatants' wigs would often be dislodged in the proceedings and could then be observed rolling around on the lawn, an odd and comic sight.

It’s most common usage is “there’ll be wigs on the green [if XYZ]…” as a warning or a prediction that an altercation will occur if condition XYZ is satisfied.

“Green” is a byword for park in Ireland (see, e.g., St. Stephen’s Green)
